title: What we repeat
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which habit of yours are you trying to heal, and whose was it first?
I said: there is a quote I really like. As adults, we try to develop the character traits that would have rescued our parents. I asked: what does that mean?

A student said: we become the adults who would have protected them. Same with your children. I said: yes, there is a role reversal, a classic psychological case, in vulnerability that we developed because we had parents in a destructive cycle.
We look for relationships that feel familiar, I said. We don't go to what is good for us, because that is strange. We go to what is familiar, because we are trying to understand it.
I said that one of the mugs I write quotes on says: is that really my belief? My children say: can you please stop. I said: identifying is key. This isn't me. This is a trauma I'm reacting to.

Psychologists say one way to heal is to go back to that ten-year-old, recognize it, and reinvent it, I said. Say: that was wrong, I was defenseless, now I realize it. This is how I'm going to break the cycle.
Another saying I like: if you never heal from what hurt you, you will bleed on the people who didn't cut you. People suffer around you from wounds you had years ago.
What are you replacing the old picture with?
Education, not advice. If this is heavy for you, a trained person can help.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a pattern you notice in your relationships.
Write whose pattern it was first, if you know.
Write the sentence you will say to yourself: is that really my belief?
Write a time you were successful that you can recall.
Write who you could talk to if this is heavy.

check.q: What did I say we are trying to develop as adults, in the saying I like?
choices: The traits that would have rescued our parents

check.q: What question is on my mug?
What did I say we go to rather than what is good for us?

recap: Notice your patterns. Ask: is that really my belief? Seek a trained person if it is heavy.
